source_refs.raw_quote: In previous reports, it has been confirmed that there are notable differences between button cells and pouch cells under same testing conditions. $^{23}$ Therefore, in order to verify the feasibility of additives for commercial SIBs, pouch NFM/HC cells were used to evaluate the performance of different functional electrolytes. The rate and cycling tests of the cells at room temperature were conducted first, and the corresponding results are shown in Figure 2a,b. It can be seen that the MS- and MBS-containing cells show lower capacity than the cells with baseline and TMBS-containing electrolyte. Similar results were also observed in the cycling tests and the inferior Coulombic efficiency of MBS- and MS-containing cells. These results indicate that the EEI induced by MS or MBS is continuously broken and repaired during the cycling, leading to worse cycling performance than the cells with TMBS or baseline electrolytes. Figure 2c shows that the cycling performance differences of the cells with TMBS are more pronounced at lower temperatures. The capacity retention of the cells with TMBS is still high at 90% after 120 cycles, while the performance of the cells with other electrolytes sharply decays owing to the fluctuating Coulombic efficiency.

source_refs.raw_quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

ABSTRACT: A functional electrolyte with trimethylsiloxybenzenesulfonate (TMBS) multigroup additive is developed to enhance the performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) from 60 to $-30^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the additive-free baseline electrolyte or the electrolytes containing monofunctional methylmethanesulfonate (MS) and methylbenzenesulfonate (MBS) additives, TMBS is more conducive to suppress the excessive side reactions at the anode and promoting the formation of robust cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI) over a wide temperature range. TMBS-containing cells exhibit enhanced performance in overdischarge testing at $60^{\circ}C$ , rate capability and cycling stability at $45^{\circ}C$ , discharge performance at $-30^{\circ}C$ , as well as low-temperature cycling stability at $-10^{\circ}C$ . Besides, this work provides an effective additive design principle for pouch NFM/HC SIBs.

KEYWORDS: sodium-ion batteries, additive, rate performance, all-climate, trimethylsiloxybenzenesulfonate

Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. 2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

source_refs.raw_quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance.

source_refs.raw_quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

source_refs.raw_quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

ABSTRACT: A functional electrolyte with trimethylsiloxybenzenesulfonate (TMBS) multigroup additive is developed to enhance the performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) from 60 to $-30^{\circ}C$ . TMBS-containing cells exhibit enhanced performance in overdischarge testing at $60^{\circ}C$ , rate capability and cycling stability at $45^{\circ}C$ , discharge performance at $-30^{\circ}C$ , as well as low-temperature cycling stability at $-10^{\circ}C$ . Besides, this work provides an effective additive design principle for pouch NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: The main raw materials (sodium salt, solvents, and additives), including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and $NaPF_{6}$ , were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. TMBS was synthesized via a one-pot method combined with in situ vacuum distillation, as shown in Figure S1. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in mixed solvents of EC:EMC = 3:7 to a concentration of 1 mol $L^{-1}$ . Considering the cost and usual dosage, the concentrations of all additives were 1%. The cathode material NFM was obtained from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd., and anode material HC was purchased from Kuraray Co., Ltd. Pouch cells was assembled with an NFM cathode (121 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), an HC anode (293 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and a Celgard 2700. The NFM cathodes were prepared by the slurry with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2 for NFM active material/polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF)/carbon nanotube (CNT)/conductive carbon black (Super P)/maleic acid. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene–butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then, the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the HC anode. The areal loadings of the NFM cathode and HC anode were 33 g $m^{-2}$ and 16 g $m^{-2}$ , respectively.

citations.quote: In this work, TMBS was synthesized via a one-pot method and developed as a bifunctional film-forming electrolyte additive to enhance the long-cycle stability of the NFM/HC cells. The capacity retention of TMBS-containing cells after 100 cycles at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ increased from $0\%$ (baseline electrolyte) to $90\%$ , and both the rate capacity and cycling stability improved greatly as well. citations.quote: In previous reports, it has been confirmed that there are notable differences between button cells and pouch cells under same testing conditions. $^{23}$ Therefore, in order to verify the feasibility of additives for commercial SIBs, pouch NFM/HC cells were used to evaluate the performance of different functional electrolytes. The rate and cycling tests of the cells at room temperature were conducted first, and the corresponding results are shown in Figure 2a,b. It can be seen that the MS- and MBS-containing cells show lower capacity than the cells with baseline and TMBS-containing electrolyte. Similar results were also observed in the cycling tests and the inferior Coulombic efficiency of MBS- and MS-containing cells. These results indicate that the EEI induced by MS or MBS is continuously broken and repaired during the cycling, leading to worse cycling performance than the cells with TMBS or baseline electrolytes. Figure 2c shows that the cycling performance differences of the cells with TMBS are more pronounced at lower temperatures. The capacity retention of the cells with TMBS is still high at 90% after 120 cycles, while the performance of the cells with other electrolytes sharply decays owing to the fluctuating Coulombic efficiency.

citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

citations.chunk_id: 0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec2::child0
citations.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

citations.quote: Stable discharge can be achieved at low-temperature rate, reflecting low-temperature adaptability. Fig. 3(a) shows the capacity stabilization effect of TMSBS on the electrolyte at different rates at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . TMSBS electrolyte maintains stable performance under $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ cycling, while the Baseline electrolyte exhibits rapid decay (Fig. S7b). Besides, The extreme low-temperature discharge experiment at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 3b) showed that the cells with TMSBS electrolyte had a capacity of 879, 853, and $814\mathrm{mAh}$ at 0.2, 0.3, and $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), while the cells with Baseline electrolyte had a capacity of 801, 752, and $716\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively (Fig. 3c). In other words, at low temperatures, TMSBS can provide higher electrolyte energy density and achieve greater capacity retention, making it suitable for emergency powering of energy storage devices in extremely cold conditions. The rate performance of SIBs at room temperature is crucial for evaluating their performance in practical applications. High-rate-performance batteries can rapidly charge and discharge in a short period of time, which is particularly important for devices that require high power output, such as electric vehicles and mobile devices [23,36].

The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.quote: With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling. Besides, rate performance of pouch cells is also improved by the synergistic effect of NP or NB electrolyte even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , as shown in Fig. 4d and S5b. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. 2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

association_citations.quote: The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first. Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

evidence_ledger.quote: The main raw materials (sodium salt, solvents, and additives), including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and $NaPF_{6}$ , were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. TMBS was synthesized via a one-pot method combined with in situ vacuum distillation, as shown in Figure S1. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in mixed solvents of EC:EMC = 3:7 to a concentration of 1 mol $L^{-1}$ . Considering the cost and usual dosage, the concentrations of all additives were 1%. The cathode material NFM was obtained from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd., and anode material HC was purchased from Kuraray Co., Ltd. Pouch cells was assembled with an NFM cathode (121 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), an HC anode (293 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and a Celgard 2700. The NFM cathodes were prepared by the slurry with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2 for NFM active material/polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF)/carbon nanotube (CNT)/conductive carbon black (Super P)/maleic acid. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene–butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then, the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the HC anode. The areal loadings of the NFM cathode and HC anode were 33 g $m^{-2}$ and 16 g $m^{-2}$ , respectively.

evidence_ledger.quote: In this work, TMBS was synthesized via a one-pot method and developed as a bifunctional film-forming electrolyte additive to enhance the long-cycle stability of the NFM/HC cells. The capacity retention of TMBS-containing cells after 100 cycles at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ increased from $0\%$ (baseline electrolyte) to $90\%$ , and both the rate capacity and cycling stability improved greatly as well. The performance enhancement of the cells with the TMBS-containing electrolyte is ascribed to the suppression of excessive side reactions at the anode and the formation of robust CEI. This work also provides an effective electrolyte design strategy for the application of all-climate SIBs.

evidence_ledger.quote: In previous reports, it has been confirmed that there are notable differences between button cells and pouch cells under same testing conditions. $^{23}$ Therefore, in order to verify the feasibility of additives for commercial SIBs, pouch NFM/HC cells were used to evaluate the performance of different functional electrolytes. The rate and cycling tests of the cells at room temperature were conducted first, and the corresponding results are shown in Figure 2a,b. It can be seen that the MS- and MBS-containing cells show lower capacity than the cells with baseline and TMBS-containing electrolyte. Similar results were also observed in the cycling tests and the inferior Coulombic efficiency of MBS- and MS-containing cells. These results indicate that the EEI induced by MS or MBS is continuously broken and repaired during the cycling, leading to worse cycling performance than the cells with TMBS or baseline electrolytes. Figure 2c shows that the cycling performance differences of the cells with TMBS are more pronounced at lower temperatures. The capacity retention of the cells with TMBS is still high at 90% after 120 cycles, while the performance of the cells with other electrolytes sharply decays owing to the fluctuating Coulombic efficiency.

The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. evidence_ledger.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

ABSTRACT: A functional electrolyte with trimethylsiloxybenzenesulfonate (TMBS) multigroup additive is developed to enhance the performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) from 60 to $-30^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the additive-free baseline electrolyte or the electrolytes containing monofunctional methylmethanesulfonate (MS) and methylbenzenesulfonate (MBS) additives, TMBS is more conducive to suppress the excessive side reactions at the anode and promoting the formation of robust cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI) over a wide temperature range. TMBS-containing cells exhibit enhanced performance in overdischarge testing at $60^{\circ}C$ , rate capability and cycling stability at $45^{\circ}C$ , discharge performance at $-30^{\circ}C$ , as well as low-temperature cycling stability at $-10^{\circ}C$ . Besides, this work provides an effective additive design principle for pouch NFM/HC SIBs.

KEYWORDS: sodium-ion batteries, additive, rate performance, all-climate, trimethylsiloxybenzenesulfonate

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

evidence_ledger.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. citations.quote: The main raw materials (sodium salt, solvents, and additives), including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and $NaPF_{6}$ , were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. TMBS was synthesized via a one-pot method combined with in situ vacuum distillation, as shown in Figure S1. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in mixed solvents of EC:EMC = 3:7 to a concentration of 1 mol $L^{-1}$ . Considering the cost and usual dosage, the concentrations of all additives were 1%. The cathode material NFM was obtained from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd., and anode material HC was purchased from Kuraray Co., Ltd. Pouch cells was assembled with an NFM cathode (121 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), an HC anode (293 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and a Celgard 2700. The NFM cathodes were prepared by the slurry with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2 for NFM active material/polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF)/carbon nanotube (CNT)/conductive carbon black (Super P)/maleic acid. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene–butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then, the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the HC anode. The areal loadings of the NFM cathode and HC anode were 33 g $m^{-2}$ and 16 g $m^{-2}$ , respectively.

Multi-Group Functional Additive Enhances the Wide-Temperature-Range Performance of Sodium-Ion Batteries
Weizhen Fan, Jian Cai, Wenlian Wang, Litao Shi, and Junmin Nan\*

![](images/ac02fb2b3f43d9340923ff0ae1a71210e9a85608741681318bf0878c1550a729.jpg)

ABSTRACT: A functional electrolyte with trimethylsiloxybenzenesulfonate (TMBS) multigroup additive is developed to enhance the performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) from 60 to $-30^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the additive-free baseline electrolyte or the electrolytes containing monofunctional methylmethanesulfonate (MS) and methylbenzenesulfonate (MBS) additives, TMBS is more conducive to suppress the excessive side reactions at the anode and promoting the formation of robust cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI) over a wide temperature range. TMBS-containing cells exhibit enhanced performance in overdischarge testing at $60^{\circ}C$ , rate capability and cycling stability at $45^{\circ}C$ , discharge performance at $-30^{\circ}C$ , as well as low-temperature cycling stability at $-10^{\circ}C$ . Besides, this work provides an effective additive design principle for pouch NFM/HC SIBs.

ABSTRACT: A functional electrolyte with trimethylsiloxybenzenesulfonate (TMBS) multigroup additive is developed to enhance the performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) from 60 to $-30^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the additive-free baseline electrolyte or the electrolytes containing monofunctional methylmethanesulfonate (MS) and methylbenzenesulfonate (MBS) additives, TMBS is more conducive to suppress the excessive side reactions at the anode and promoting the formation of robust cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI) over a wide temperature range. TMBS-containing cells exhibit enhanced performance in overdischarge testing at $60^{\circ}C$ , rate capability and cycling stability at $45^{\circ}C$ , discharge performance at $-30^{\circ}C$ , as well as low-temperature cycling stability at $-10^{\circ}C$ . Besides, this work provides an effective additive design principle for pouch NFM/HC SIBs.

The rate and cycling tests of the cells at room temperature were conducted first, and the corresponding results are shown in Figure 2a,b. It can be seen that the MS- and MBS-containing cells show lower capacity than the cells with baseline and TMBS-containing electrolyte. Similar results were also observed in the cycling tests and the inferior Coulombic efficiency of MBS- and MS-containing cells. These results indicate that the EEI induced by MS or MBS is continuously broken and repaired during the cycling, leading to worse cycling performance than the cells with TMBS or baseline electrolytes. Figure 2c shows that the cycling performance differences of the cells with TMBS are more pronounced at lower temperatures. The capacity retention of the cells with TMBS is still high at 90% after 120 cycles, while the performance of the cells with other electrolytes sharply decays owing to the fluctuating Coulombic efficiency.

NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. citations.chunk_id: 0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec2::child0
citations.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

Besides, The extreme low-temperature discharge experiment at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 3b) showed that the cells with TMSBS electrolyte had a capacity of 879, 853, and $814\mathrm{mAh}$ at 0.2, 0.3, and $0.5\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), while the cells with Baseline electrolyte had a capacity of 801, 752, and $716\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively (Fig. 3c). In other words, at low temperatures, TMSBS can provide higher electrolyte energy density and achieve greater capacity retention, making it suitable for emergency powering of energy storage devices in extremely cold conditions. The rate performance of SIBs at room temperature is crucial for evaluating their performance in practical applications. High-rate-performance batteries can rapidly charge and discharge in a short period of time, which is particularly important for devices that require high power output, such as electric vehicles and mobile devices [23,36].

In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

citations.quote: In summary, “hard-soft synergy” strategy—reasonably coupling NaDFP with TMSP or TMSB as the functional electrolytes successfully achieved wide-temperature performance of pouch SIBs over a range of $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Benefit to the high-quality and rich element optimized NaDFP-based CEI/SEI layers on the electrode surfaces, and optimizing electrolyte structure which decrease the desolvation energy and induce superior electrolyte properties, a high capacity retention of $92\%$ after 350 cycles and a stable cycling performance at $1\mathrm{C}$ were achieved even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Besides, both the discharge capacity at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ were also greatly improved. Importantly, only tiny dose of NaDFP, TMSB/TMSP with reasonably couple could enable considerably effective performance improvement of SIBs, which is essential to reduce the cost and advance the commercialization. This work not only obtains functional electrolytes for enhanced wide-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs, but also sheds lights on the designing multi-functional additive electrolytes of SIBs.

Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

citations.quote: The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first. Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ .

3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

ABSTRACT: A functional electrolyte with trimethylsiloxybenzenesulfonate (TMBS) multigroup additive is developed to enhance the performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) from 60 to $-30^{\circ}C$ . citations.quote: In previous reports, it has been confirmed that there are notable differences between button cells and pouch cells under same testing conditions. $^{23}$ Therefore, in order to verify the feasibility of additives for commercial SIBs, pouch NFM/HC cells were used to evaluate the performance of different functional electrolytes. The rate and cycling tests of the cells at room temperature were conducted first, and the corresponding results are shown in Figure 2a,b. It can be seen that the MS- and MBS-containing cells show lower capacity than the cells with baseline and TMBS-containing electrolyte. Similar results were also observed in the cycling tests and the inferior Coulombic efficiency of MBS- and MS-containing cells. These results indicate that the EEI induced by MS or MBS is continuously broken and repaired during the cycling, leading to worse cycling performance than the cells with TMBS or baseline electrolytes. Figure 2c shows that the cycling performance differences of the cells with TMBS are more pronounced at lower temperatures. The capacity retention of the cells with TMBS is still high at 90% after 120 cycles, while the performance of the cells with other electrolytes sharply decays owing to the fluctuating Coulombic efficiency.

citations.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

## 配方筛选结果
已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。

### 候选资料：candidate-1-tmbs（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=3, EMC=7；添加剂：TMBS；添加剂用量：TMBS=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0018_Fan 等 - 2026 - Multi-Group Functional Additive Enhances the Wide-Temperature-Range Performance of Sodium-Ion Batter::sec3::child0]：The main raw materials (sodium salt, solvents, and additives), including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and $NaPF_{6}$ , were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. TMBS was synthesized via a one-pot method combined with in situ vacuum distillation, as shown in Figure S1. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in mixed solvents of EC:EMC = 3:7 to a concentration of 1 mol $L^{-1}$ . Considering the cost and usual dosage, the concentrations of all additives were 1%. The cathode material NFM was obtained from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd., and anode material HC was purchased from Kuraray Co., Ltd. Pouch cells was assembled with an NFM cathode (121 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), an HC anode (293 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and a Celgard 2700. The NFM cathodes were prepared by the slurry with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2 for NFM active material/polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF)/carbon nanotube (CNT)/conductive carbon black (Super P)/maleic acid. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene–butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then, the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the HC anode. The areal loadings of the NFM cathode and HC anode were 33 g $m^{-2}$ and 16 g $m^{-2}$ , respectively.

### 候选资料：candidate-2-tmsbs（尚未获推荐）
